key_insight: The paper introduces symbolic property analysis for DRL agents, enabling verification over ranges of system states (not just single point inputs) so practitioners can reason about agent behavior and safety across realistic operating conditions.
problem_solved: Existing verification methods check DRL policies at fixed input points, providing limited coverage and missing failure modes that occur across ranges of system and network states; this work addresses the need for scalable, range-based guarantees.
method: Define a compact symbolic property language to express constraints over ranges of inputs, system parameters, and expected policy outputs/behaviors.

Use abstraction and solver-driven analysis (e.g., interval/reachability techniques and constraint solving) to verify whether a DRL policy satisfies those symbolic properties across continuous regions of state space.

Validate the approach on representative systems-and-networking tasks (e.g., adaptive streaming, wireless resource management, congestion control) to locate unsafe regions and improve test/repair focus.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a practical way to obtain broader, more actionable safety and robustness guarantees for DRL controllers in networking and systems, enabling targeted testing, debugging, and safer deployment.
visual_elements: Concept diagram: a box representing an input/state range mapped through the DRL policy to output behavior, highlighting symbolic property boundaries.
Pipeline flowchart: specify symbolic property → abstraction/solver analysis → verification result (safe/unsafe) → targeted mitigation.
State-space heatmap: safe vs. unsafe regions discovered by symbolic analysis over system parameters (color-coded).
Bar/line chart: comparison of coverage and detected failures between point-based verification and symbolic-range verification.
paper_title: Analyzing Symbolic Properties for DRL Agents in Systems and Networking
paper_authors: Mohammad Zangooei, Jannis Weil, Amr Rizk, Mina Tahmasbi Arashloo, Raouf Boutaba
